report.summary: Reviewed harness.py chunk 1: docstring claims vs code; several claims kept, one broken (eval_task_tier1 can raise KeyError on missing 'repo'), others uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, imports, task/row helpers, Tier 1 evaluation functions.

symbols.name: _IGNORE_DIRS
symbols.note: Set of directory names skipped for whole-repo concat (context B).

symbols.name: _task_error_row
symbols.note: Builds a row for resolution failures; includes 'error' key, no recall/compression keys.

symbols.name: _correctness_task_row
symbols.note: Builds an error row for correctness tasks; sets correctness_task=True.

symbols.name: _is_focus_withheld
symbols.note: Returns True if any withheld entry has role 'focus'.

symbols.name: _focus_withheld_row
symbols.note: Builds a row for focus-withheld tasks; includes focus_withheld=True, no recall/compression keys.

symbols.name: _recall
symbols.note: Returns (fraction of must_include found, missed list); empty list gives 1.0.

symbols.name: eval_task_tier1
symbols.note: Deterministic Tier-1 result for a single task; catches ValueError/OSError, refuses correctness tasks.

symbols.name: _tier1_aggregate
symbols.note: Aggregates Tier-1 rows: n_tasks, mean_recall, mean_compression, n_slice_recall_misses, missed_ids.

symbols.name: run_tier1
symbols.note: Runs Tier 1 over tasks (default TASKS); body beyond chunk.

claims.text: Tier 1 (deterministic, no LLM, the rigorous core): For each task, take the distilled ``semantic_slice`` and measure * recall = fraction of ``must_include`` found in the slice text, * compression = 1 - slice_tokens / whole_repo_tokens.
claims.why: eval_task_tier1 computes recall via _recall and compression as 1 - slice_tokens/whole_repo_tokens.

claims.text: Aggregated PER LABEL-PROVENANCE TIER (see ``daedalus.eval.tasks`` docstring) -- never blended into one number
claims.why: run_tier1 uses _by_provenance which aggregates per (provenance, tier) bucket; no top-level blended mean in this chunk.

claims.text: ``tier == "quarantine"`` tasks are excluded from every headline and reported separately (see ``run_tier1``)
claims.why: run_tier1 body is not in this chunk; no evidence of headline exclusion here.

claims.text: Any task with recall < 1.0 is a *slice-recall miss*; we surface exactly which symbols were dropped -- that is the feedback signal the structcore team uses to sharpen slices.
claims.why: _tier1_aggregate computes n_slice_recall_misses and missed_ids; eval_task_tier1 includes 'missed' list.

claims.text: Arms A/B/C (deterministic, no LLM -- same honesty rules as Tier 1): ... scored on BOTH recall (via ``_recall``) and true token cost.
claims.why: Arms functions are not in this chunk; no code to verify.

claims.text: Tier 2 (opt-in, needs a runtime): ... Gated: if no provider is reachable it is skipped cleanly with a message -- Tier 2 NEVER crashes Tier 1 and NEVER makes a network call unless explicitly enabled.
claims.why: Tier 2 functions are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Gate (advisory, local-only): ``run_gate`` replays the corpus against a stored ``baseline.json`` and flags PRIMARY-tier tasks whose recall decreased -- see its docstring for the exact workflow. ADVISORY ONLY: never wired to block an autonomous action; there is no CI in this repo, this is a developer-run local check.
claims.why: run_gate is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Isolated: imports only structcore's stable public API.
claims.why: Imports from daedalus.structcore are index, languages, parse, slice, and tokens; all appear to be public API modules.

claims.text: The hardcoded ``TASKS`` plus every task persisted in the mint store (``daedalus.eval.mint.load_minted_tasks``) -- the load path that closes the mint -> quarantine -> confirm -> primary flywheel ... no store file -> ``load_minted_tasks`` returns ``[]`` -> this is exactly ``TASKS``, same order, same content.
claims.why: all_tasks returns TASKS + load_minted_tasks(); if load_minted_tasks returns [], the result is TASKS in same order.

claims.text: This is the default every ``run_*``/``*_baseline`` function below uses in place of ``TASKS``
claims.why: Other run_* functions not in this chunk; cannot verify they use all_tasks.

claims.text: Fail-closed: only the EXACT string "primary" counts. A missing, typo'd, or otherwise unrecognized tier is treated as quarantine (excluded from any go/no-go number)
claims.why: Function returns label_tier == 'primary'; anything else returns False, which _group_rows_by_provenance maps to 'quarantine'.

claims.text: {provenance: {"primary": [...], "quarantine": [...]}} for every provenance actually present in ``rows``. Both tier buckets always exist (possibly empty)
claims.why: Initializes out[prov] = {'primary': [], 'quarantine': []} for each provenance, then appends.

claims.text: This is the ONLY aggregation path Tier 1 and the arms comparison use -- there is deliberately no top-level blended mean anywhere in this module.
claims.why: Arms comparison is not in this chunk; cannot verify no other aggregation path exists.

claims.text: CALLERS MUST PRE-FILTER OUT ERRORED ROWS (``"error" in row``) AND FOCUS-WITHHELD ROWS (``row.get("focus_withheld")``) before passing ``rows`` here -- see ``run_tier1``/``run_arms``. Neither carries a recall/compression measurement, so folding either in would either KeyError or (worse) silently get treated as a zero, corrupting the mean it was supposed to be excluded from.
claims.why: The aggregation functions (_mean) would KeyError on missing recall/compression keys, as claimed; error and focus_withheld rows have no such keys.

claims.text: Shared shape for a per-task RESOLUTION failure -- ``ValueError`` (unindexable target, e.g. a quarantined mint task whose file was renamed/deleted after minting, or an unresolvable ``repo`` label) or ``OSError`` (repo unreadable). Used by every ``eval_task_*``/``run_*`` per-task try block so one malformed task degrades to a single reported row instead of crashing the whole eval run -- "a quarantined flywheel task must not be able to take down the go/no-go machinery."
claims.why: eval_task_tier1 catches (ValueError, OSError) and returns _task_error_row; the row has 'error' key and no recall/compression.

claims.text: ``error`` is the marker every downstream aggregator/report checks (``"error" in row`` or ``row.get("error")``). There is deliberately no ``recall``/``compression`` (or arms ``recall_A``/``tokens_A``/...) key at all -- ABSENT, not ``None`` -- so any aggregation path that forgets to filter on ``error`` fails loudly (``KeyError``) instead of silently averaging in a placeholder.
claims.why: The returned dict has no recall/compression keys; _tier1_aggregate would KeyError if passed such rows.

claims.text: A FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS task ... carries no ``must_include``, so handing it to ``_recall`` would return the vacuous 1.0 -- a task that cannot fail, inflating the go/no-go number with a measurement that never happened. That is the precise failure the tier machinery exists to prevent, so it is refused here rather than averaged in.
claims.why: eval_task_tier1 calls _correctness_task_row before slicing; _recall would return 1.0 for empty must_include, as described.

claims.text: Refused as an ERRORED row (``error`` key present, no ``recall``/``compression`` key at all) so it takes every existing path for a degraded measurement: excluded from all aggregates, listed in ``errored``, never silently dropped, and LOUD in ``run_gate`` when its tier is primary.
claims.why: run_gate and errored listing are not in this chunk.

claims.text: True iff ``semantic_slice`` fail-closed on the task's OWN focus file (see slice.py's FOCUS GATE): the withheld block contains a role=="focus" entry -- the exact shape slice.py emits when the unconditional secret floor fires on the target itself, not on some neighbour it dropped.
claims.why: Function checks res.get('withheld') for any entry with role == 'focus'.

claims.text: Shared shape for a FOCUS-WITHHELD row -- the fence fail-closed on the task's own focus file, a lane A1 label-hygiene case distinct from ``_task_error_row``: ``semantic_slice`` did not raise (this is not a resolution failure), it legitimately returned an empty, gate-refused slice. There is NO recall/compression/missed (Tier 1) or recall_A/tokens_A/... (arms) key at all -- ABSENT, not a zero -- same "any aggregator that forgets to filter fails loudly" contract as the ``error`` marker, keyed here on ``focus_withheld`` instead.
claims.why: The returned dict has focus_withheld=True and no recall/compression keys; _is_focus_withheld is called before recall calculation.

claims.text: Fraction of ``must_include`` found (substring) in ``slice_text``, plus the list of items that were missed. Empty label list -> recall 1.0 vacuously.
claims.why: Function returns 1.0, [] if must_include is empty; otherwise computes found/total and missed list.

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: a resolution failure -- ``semantic_slice``/``resolve_task_repo`` raising ``ValueError`` (e.g. the task's ``target`` is not in the index, the live repro that motivated this: a minted quarantine task whose target file had moved), or ``OSError`` reading the repo -- is caught and returned as an ERRORED row (``_task_error_row``) instead of propagating.
claims.why: The try block covers resolve_task_repo and semantic_slice, catching only ValueError and OSError. However, task['repo'] is an unguarded subscript that will raise KeyError if the key is missing (line 96), and task['id']/task['target'] are also unguarded in the success path (lines 119, 121). The docstring claims NEVER RAISES, but a malformed task dict missing 'repo' would raise KeyError, not be caught.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is refused here before anything is sliced -- see ``_correctness_task_row``.
claims.why: is_correctness_task(task) is checked first; if true, returns _correctness_task_row(task).

claims.text: Defaulted so pre-provenance task dicts (e.g. ad-hoc test fixtures that predate this schema) still group as "hand_reachable"/"primary" -- additive, byte-identical aggregation for callers who never adopted the new fields.
claims.why: label_provenance defaults to 'hand_reachable', label_tier defaults to 'primary' via task.get.

observations.what: eval_task_tier1 accesses task['repo'] unguarded; if absent raises KeyError, contradicting NEVER RAISES.
eval_task_tier1 success path accesses task['id'] and task['target'] unguarded; missing keys would raise KeyError.
The module docstring says 'NEVER makes a network call unless explicitly enabled' for Tier 2, but the chunk contains no Tier 2 code.
The docstring for _by_provenance instructs callers to pre-filter error/focus rows, but no enforcement in this function; a caller could forget, causing KeyError in aggregation.
